definition: Vintage is the calendar year in which a REC's underlying generation occurred. RPS rules typically restrict how long after its vintage year a REC can still be used to satisfy compliance obligations — the source gives an example of a three-year usability window.
core_idea: Vintage functions like a shelf life or expiration window governing how long a REC remains eligible for compliance use.
key_points: Vintage = the year the REC's underlying generation took place
RPS programs typically define a maximum eligibility age for compliance use (example given: within three years of generation)
